title: Scenario Diffusion: Controllable Driving Scenario Generation With Diffusion

control_signal.value: Map image plus agent tokens (e.g. position, heading, size, speed, final speed, trajectory curvature for chosen agents) and a global scene token that sets how many extra agents are generated.

control_mechanism.value: Map encoded and channel-concatenated with the noisy latent; tokens embedded by per-type MLPs and used as keys/values in U-Net cross-attention. Random token masking during training (partial tokenization) lets the model fill in extra agents.

base_model.value: Latent diffusion: VAE autoencoder trained for anchor-free detection of oriented boxes plus trajectory regression from BEV; conditional U-Net denoiser trained with the EDM algorithm.

datasets.value: Argoverse 2 motion forecasting (250,000 scenarios, 6 regions) and an internal dataset of 6 million scenarios from Las Vegas, Seattle, San Francisco and SLAC campus.

metrics.value: Agent token match rate, number of additional generated agents, MMD-based distribution metrics, precision/recall/F1 of token matching, earth mover's distance on agent count, cross-region comparisons over 5 seeds.

controllability_evidence.value: Agent token match rate stays 0.97 (0.01) from 0% to 50% masking and 0.96 at 90%; extra generated agents rise from 0.4 (0.3) to 12.6 (0.7) as masking probability increases, showing the global token controls density.

stated_limitations.value: Broader generalization needs more work; training assumes bounding-box perception and trajectory models; only on-road vehicles modelled (no pedestrians); may need iterative generation over larger regions as AV moves.

notes: MMD metric values are only partly visible in packet tables.
